note: Fictional GW-* assets mapped to real AEP Texas / ERCOT and City of Corpus Christi Water topology. All entity names, system IDs and personnel are fictional. Physical locations, voltage classes and pipeline routes follow public infrastructure records.

entities.name: Coastal Bend Power & Water Authority
entities.note: Fictional combined electric-and-water operator standing in for the real mix of AEP Texas / ERCOT (grid) and City of Corpus Christi Water Department (water). Operates the substations and water treatment assets below under a single SCADA umbrella.

entities.name: Meridian Controls Corp
entities.note: Fictional OT vendor. Supplies the SCADA master station, RTUs and historian used by CBPWA.

entities.name: ClearPath Network Solutions
entities.note: Fictional VPN / remote-access vendor. Supplies GW-SYS-JMP-01, the jump host used for remote relay configuration and historian access.

facilities.name: Riverside Switching Station
facilities.real_analog: White Point Energy Center substation (AEP Texas / ERCOT, 345/138 kV transmission interconnect, north shore of Corpus Christi Bay)
facilities.note: Primary 345-kV import point for the Corpus Christi peninsula; loss here causes cascading load-shedding on the south side.

facilities.name: Harbor View Substation
facilities.real_analog: Nueces Bay substation (138/69 kV, northwest Corpus Christi)
facilities.note: Feeds the northwest industrial and residential load. Trip propagates to Harbor Bridge and port distribution feeders.

facilities.name: Crosstown Substation
facilities.real_analog: Highway 9 substation (138/69 kV, central Corpus Christi)
facilities.note: Central peninsula substation feeding Districts 3 and 4. Loss contributes to water-pressure drop because it backs up FAC-UTL-01 auxiliary pumps.

facilities.name: Southside Substation
facilities.real_analog: Westside substation (138/69 kV, west Corpus Christi / Calallen corridor)
facilities.note: Serves west-side residential and the Calallen corridor. Last of the four affected substations to show modified relay configurations.

facilities.name: Bayside Substation
facilities.real_analog: Oso Creek substation (138 kV, south Corpus Christi)
facilities.note: South-side substation; not compromised but used as the unaffected comparison baseline in the outage-footprint analysis.

facilities.name: Palisade Energy Center
facilities.real_analog: Barney M. Davis Power Plant (gas turbine, Corpus Christi north shore, ~384 MW nameplate)
facilities.note: Local peaking unit; dispatched during storm restoration but cannot compensate for relay trips at GW-FAC-SUB-01 alone.

facilities.name: Texana Booster Station 1
facilities.real_analog: Mary Rhodes Pipeline Phase I — Pump Station 1 (Lake Texana, Edna TX, start of 101-mile raw-water pipeline)
facilities.note: Lifts raw water from Lake Texana into the Mary Rhodes Phase I pipeline. Not on the CBPWA SCADA but feeds FAC-UTL-01 raw water supply.

facilities.name: Texana Booster Station 2
facilities.real_analog: Mary Rhodes Pipeline Phase I — Pump Station 2 (mid-route booster, ~50 miles from Lake Texana)
facilities.note: Mid-route booster on Phase I pipeline. Manual backup if SCADA is unavailable.

facilities.name: Colorado River Booster Station
facilities.real_analog: Mary Rhodes Pipeline Phase II — Booster Pump Station (near Bay City TX; 42-mile pipeline from Colorado River diversion to 6-MG ground storage tank; fiber-optic SCADA comms)
facilities.note: Phase II booster. Its historian logs unauthorized setpoint changes on D+23 — a key detection artifact for T9.

facilities.name: Northwest Storage Tank 1
facilities.note: One of 9 distribution storage tanks; first to drop below 50% on D+10 due to pump-pressure reduction.

systems.name: Meridian SCADA Master Station
systems.note: Controls relay settings and breaker operations at all five substations and pump setpoints at FAC-UTL-01, GW-FAC-WTR-01 to WTR-03. Alarm history is stored in the Meridian historian (GW-SYS-HST-01).

systems.name: Meridian Historian
systems.note: Stores all SCADA tag values and alarm events. The D+23 unauthorized setpoint change at GW-FAC-WTR-03 is preserved here and is a primary detection artifact.

systems.name: ClearPath VPN Gateway
systems.note: Remote-access jump host used by CBPWA field engineers to configure relays and push SCADA setpoints. Session logs show 14 authenticated sessions from non-Texas IP blocks during D-3 to D+28.
